source_text_delivery.delivery_output_caps: Successful text batches requested inner exec_command output caps of 4000-8500 tokens and remained within outer 10000-token output cap. Source text was emitted as contiguous chunks of at most 6000 characters.
source_text_delivery.initial_summary_delivery_repair: An initial combined nine-chunk summary call exceeded the outer output cap and was visibly truncated in its middle. The affected 18000:36000 range was re-delivered as three complete 6000-character chunks in a subsequent 7000-token inner call. The original initial call's complete 0:18000 and 36000:53736 portions plus the repaired middle cover the full snapshot. No truncated middle was treated as read.
source_text_delivery.end_checks: Exact character counts and full hashes verified; final source tails explicitly checked and retained. Contiguous chunk ends equal source character counts; line counts were not used as completeness evidence.

pdf_inspection.native_text: Both assigned PDFs opened with fitz. All native text was compared to the fully delivered extraction after removing extraction page wrappers and whitespace; equality holds for both complete documents.

image_delivery.source_hash_check_method: Read every original_file byte string and calculate SHA-1/SHA-256 and length; compare archival expected_sha1, original_sha256 and expected_size. All comparisons passed.
image_delivery.initial_method: The first 36 sheets were viewed via view_image(detail:'original') and forwarded with image(url) without the second original detail argument. Those earlier forwards are honestly retained as an incomplete transport method, not used as the final original-forwarding evidence.
image_delivery.completed_method: All fifty sheets were subsequently delivered with view_image({path: original_file, detail:'original'}) and image(result.image_url, 'original'). For the first 36 this was an explicit original reinspection; the final 14 were first delivered after the transport correction.
image_delivery.payload_check_method: Independently parse each returned view_image data URL, base64-decode the actual returned JPEG bytes, compute SHA-256, parse JPEG SOF width/height and compare the hash to the pinned original file SHA-256. A pure-JavaScript SHA-256 implementation was first checked against the known SHA-256 of abc (ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad). No original-file hash was substituted for the returned-payload calculation.
image_delivery.payload_hash_meaning: SHA-256 of the actual base64-decoded delivered JPEG content bytes, separately calculated from source-file verification. It is not a hash of the base64 string and is not a decoded RGB pixel hash. Payload byte identity with original JPEG establishes that dimensions and pixels were unchanged before forwarding.
